title: Tips, the kitty and the $17.50 wage
summary: Hinton asks about the slang for tips; Jones explains the kitty and splitting tips.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: You mentioned another thing that I'd like to have for the record, that now everybody should really
know about it. You mentioned you used to play for $17.50 a week and what you called tips kicks? I think you had a name for it.
No, you said another word - kicks are 17 and you asked did I know what it meant. We'll pass it along and we'll probably come to it later, like you got $17 a week and cups or something.
$17.50 a week - oh, spaghetti and meatballs.
You mentioned it, it was something like a tip. You didn't mention whether it was food or what it was. It was like something extra was added, $17 and cups or kicks or some word you used.
Well, naturally you had a kitty. You know everybody had a kitty. You saw that.
That's what you put the tips in, of course.

You put that in the kitty and you had the kitty up with the light in it and the people passed by - they'd just split up the kitty, you know, and you had the two sabrettes around there and you had to take them checks and shake them up because they put the stuff all down in their bosom and all that.
